answer: Give every established agent a small, slowly refilling quota of invitations, each backed by a slice of the inviter's own stake: a newcomer enters only through a sponsor who loses stake if the newcomer is proven fake. Like a sparrow that can only nest where another bird vouches for the branch, a sybil flood needs many distinct sponsors, and a gale of fake accounts drains the sponsors who enabled them. Add an oasis rule: newcomers earn nothing until they have done verifiable work attested by unrelated peers, so mass-produced identities starve before they can profit.
